acceptance.check: In the schedules list, a monthly schedule that has already had its only occurrence (ends after 1 occurrence, started today) shows an actions menu with no 'Skip next scheduled date' and no 'Restart'; a monthly schedule that repeats indefinitely still shows 'Skip next scheduled date'.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Open the Schedules page. Open the actions menu on a schedule whose recurring date reads 'for 1 occurrence' -- the one-off date is today, so it is Due. The menu lists Post transaction, Post transaction today, Complete and Delete, and no Skip or Restart. Open the actions menu on a schedule whose recurring date is indefinite; Skip next scheduled date is there. Both come from the single predicate at SchedulesTable.tsx:178, which is what this criterion pins down.

acceptance.check: Double-clicking a row in the schedules list opens exactly one edit modal, and a single Cancel returns to the schedules list with no modal left behind.
acceptance.how_to_verify: On the Schedules page, double-click a schedule row. One Schedule details modal appears, not two stacked copies. Press Cancel once. The modal is gone and the list is interactive. Before the change the two clicks each dispatched pushModal, so two modals mounted and Cancel only popped the top one, leaving the second underneath.

acceptance.check: Saving a schedule with a blank name and then reopening it for editing emits neither of React's input-control console warnings ('value prop on an input should not be null' and 'A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled').
acceptance.how_to_verify: On the Schedules page, add a schedule and clear the Name field, then save it. Click the saved row to reopen it for editing. With the browser console open, no warning about a null value prop or an uncontrolled input appears. This is the hand procedure attempt 1's AC-3 already described, and it is stated as a browser criterion because QA's Playwright cases are required to keep console capture on and to fail a case that passes while throwing console errors (.sdlc/agents/qa.md:150-152), so QA observes the console itself rather than taking the assertion on trust from a spec. The code under test is the `value={fields.name || ''}` guard at ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134, which is what makes the null name from useScheduleEdit.ts:119 safe.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make pushModal dedupe by modal name, or add a replaceModal-style guard inside the reducer.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes shared behaviour for all 231 call sites under packages/desktop-client/src, several of which legitimately stack modals (a rules modal opened from a schedule modal, for instance), and nothing in this ticket asks for it. The one-line call-site change fixes the reported bug with a precedent already in the codebase.

alternatives_considered.approach: Debounce or guard the row's onClick so a second click within a threshold is ignored.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It papers over the symptom with a timing heuristic that has to be tuned, still fires a spurious dispatch, and leaves any other double-dispatch path (keyboard Enter plus click, a fast second row) unfixed. replaceModal is deterministic.

alternatives_considered.approach: Set verify.e2e in .sdlc/config.yml so the schedules spec becomes a CI-proven acceptance criterion.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: .sdlc/config.yml is a forbidden path, and the reviewer's first objection said so explicitly. AC-3 is re-stated as a browser procedure instead, and the residual risk that the e2e suite is ungated is recorded as a fact about the repository rather than fixed here.

alternatives_considered.approach: Type the occurrence count into #end_occurrences in the page model instead of asserting the default.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The field is uncontrolled, so filling it and then asserting it reproduces exactly the tautology the reviewer rejected in AC-4 -- the test would be asserting a value it wrote. Asserting the app's own default of 1 actually exercises unparseConfig's validInterval round-trip.

alternatives_considered.approach: Scope the picker testid by adding one to the ScheduleEditForm wrapper rather than the shared RecurringSchedulePicker trigger.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The trigger is what the test needs to assert on -- the rendered recurring description -- and duplicating the attribute on a wrapper would force the test to walk up a level to read the trigger's text anyway. One attribute on the trigger, scoped at the locator, is smaller.

Note this component has two consumers, ScheduleEditForm.tsx:259 and util/GenericInput.tsx:398, so the new locator must be scoped to the schedule-edit-modal root rather than the page. (2) Add ScheduleEditModal.setRecurrenceEndAfterOccurrences() to packages/desktop-client/e2e/page-models/schedule-edit-modal.ts: it clicks the picker trigger, clicks the #repeat_end_dropdown Select, clicks the 'for' option in the open menu, then asserts #end_occurrences already reads '1' rather than typing into it -- the Input at RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:454 is uncontrolled (defaultValue={config.endOccurrences || 1}) and useScheduleEdit.ts:201 seeds endOccurrences: 1, so the assertion is checking the app's own default. (3) Rename the three nth-prefixed page-model methods in packages/desktop-client/e2e/page-models/schedules-page.ts to take a row Locator instead of a number, scope the menu locator with .last() so a left-over menu from an earlier assertion cannot make expect(menu).toBeVisible() throw on a multi-match, and add editSchedule(row) which dblclicks the row's payee cell and returns a ScheduleEditModal scoped to schedule-edit-modal. (4) In packages/desktop-client/e2e/schedules.test.ts: add an exhausted monthly (count 1, start today) fixture with no schedule name, assert its actions menu carries no Skip entry while a never-ending monthly still does, drive the exhausted schedule's edit path with setRecurrenceEndAfterOccurrences and assert the trigger shows the singular 'occurrence' description, add the double-click case, and delete the REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES self-test together with its split loop and page.evaluate probe block, narrowing the surviving console guard to React's two input warnings. The same no-name fixture serves the nullable-name edit path, because useScheduleEdit.ts:119 sets name to schedule.name ?? null on the edit path and the add path at :266 seeds null anyway. files.change: Add data-testid="recurrence-description" to the trigger Button at :627-633. One attribute, no behaviour change. This is what lets the e2e page model read the picker's rendered description (the 'for 1 occurrence' singular produced by getRecurringDescription in packages/desktop-client/src/util/schedule.ts:49-60) without matching on user-facing copy. The component has two consumers -- ScheduleEditForm.tsx:259 and util/GenericInput.tsx:398 -- so any locator for it must be scoped to a root; the schedules page model scopes to the schedule-edit-modal.
files.why: The singular/plural branch at schedule.ts:59 is unreachable from any existing test because the trigger is only identifiable by its label text. A testid is the smallest change that makes it observable, and it survives copy changes.

files.change: Add async setRecurrenceEndAfterOccurrences(): Promise<void>. It clicks this.locator.getByTestId('recurrence-description'), then the #repeat_end_dropdown Select (RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:442), then the option button whose accessible name is exactly 'for' inside the open menu. It then asserts #end_occurrences (RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx:454) reads '1' and returns -- it does not type into the field. The field is uncontrolled (defaultValue={config.endOccurrences || 1}) and useScheduleEdit.ts:201 seeds endOccurrences: 1 on the set-repeats path, so reading '1' is asserting the app's own default rather than inputting it. Scope the option lookup to the open menu and use an exact accessible-name match: 'for' is a substring of nothing else in the popover, but Playwright's getByRole name matching is substring-by-default, and 'Apply'/'indefinitely'/'until' are the only other options present.
files.why: The existing typeAndSelectOption helper cannot express this: the end-occurrences Select has no Field wrapper, so there is no data-testid to target, and the count Input is uncontrolled, so fill() would be asserting a value the test itself just wrote -- the same tautology the reviewer rejected in AC-4.

files.change: Four changes. (a) Add an exhausted-recurrence fixture to the existing test schedule: a monthly schedule starting today and ending after 1 occurrence, which yields exactly one upcoming date and therefore an exhausted recurrence, with no name field set so it also exercises the nullable-name edit path. (b) Extend the row-actions test to assert the exhausted row's menu offers no 'Skip next scheduled date' and no 'Restart' while a never-ending monthly row still offers Skip, using the new scheduleMenuHasItem/scheduleMenuItemNames names. (c) Extend the recurring-date test: dblclick the exhausted row to open it, click Repeats, call setRecurrenceEndAfterOccurrences(), Apply, and assert the trigger now reads the singular 'occurrence' description, then cancel. Add a new test that dblclicks a row and asserts exactly one schedule-edit-modal is present and that a single Cancel returns to the list. (d) Delete the console self-test in full: the REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES array at :33, the split/assert loop at :459 that re-derives those literals, and the page.evaluate block at :473-481 that injects them into the page. Narrow the surviving guard -- reactInputWarning, CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS, watchReactInputWarnings, the unconditional console drain and the final expect(messages).toEqual([]) -- to watch only React's two input warnings ('value prop on an input should not be null' and 'A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled'), with a comment saying the old list also matched the test's own probe strings and therefore could not fail on app behaviour. Keep that guard attached to every test that opens the schedule edit modal, including the new ones.
files.why: The probes are literals the test writes into the page and reads back, so that case asserts nothing about the app and gives false confidence that console capture works. The surviving drain is the guard with real value: it is what proves ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134's `value={fields.name || ''}` keeps a nameless schedule from tripping React's null-value warning, and narrowing it to exactly the two warnings the app can plausibly produce removes the self-inflicted matches.

validated_work_order.root_cause: Two independent causes. (1) Coverage gap: no e2e fixture creates a schedule whose recurrence is exhausted, so the scheduleIsRecurring-vs-scheduleIsSkippable divergence at schedules.ts:516 is never observed, and no test drives the row-click edit path for a schedule whose name is null, so the ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134 `value={fields.name || ''}` guard that useScheduleEdit.ts:119 makes necessary is never exercised. (2) Product defect: onEdit at packages/desktop-client/src/components/schedules/index.tsx:31 uses pushModal, whose only special case is the keyboard-shortcuts modal, so two rapid row clicks -- or any double-click -- append two identical 'schedule-edit' entries to modalStack; Modals.tsx:268-269 gives them distinct keys, so both render, and useModalState.onClose dispatches popModal, so a single Cancel removes only the top one. The reducer's append is deliberate for genuinely nested flows and is dispatched on 231 lines under packages/desktop-client/src, so the defect belongs at the Schedules call site, not in the reducer.

validated_work_order.understanding: QA reviewed the schedules e2e suite on attempt 1 and filed three findings, all of which survive unchanged: (1) the exhausted-recurrence skip case does not exist, and SchedulesTable.tsx:178 already gates the Skip menu item on scheduleIsSkippable(dateCond, schedule.next_date), so the fix is test coverage, not product code; (2) a schedule row is a single <tr data-testid="row"> whose onClick calls onSelect(schedule.id), and Schedules/index.tsx:28-35 dispatches pushModal for that call, so a double-click dispatches twice, appends two identical 'schedule-edit' entries to modalStack, and because Modals.tsx keys entries by `${name}-${idx}` both mount while useModalState.isActive only compares lastModal.name -- the user gets two stacked modals and one Cancel only pops the top one; (3) the console-warning self-test is a tautology -- REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES (schedules.test.ts:33) are literals the test itself injects into the page at :473-481 and then reads back at :459, so it asserts that a string it wrote is the string it wrote and proves nothing about the app; the real guard is the watchReactInputWarnings drain in the tests that open the schedule edit modal. Attempt 1 answered none of the coverage this ticket asks for and was rejected on two counts, both about verifiability rather than approach: AC-3 was marked verify:"test" while naming only an e2e case that no CI job runs (verify.e2e is "" and verify.required_checks is [], and vite.config.mts:405-428 limits vitest to src/**, so packages/desktop-client/e2e never runs in CI), and AC-4 was marked verify:"test" while naming no test case at all. This revision drops AC-4 entirely, moves the guard-narrowing requirement onto the files[] entry for schedules.test.ts as prose, and re-states AC-3 as verify:"browser". The technical approach is otherwise unchanged from the attempt the reviewer did not object to.
unknowns: Whether the double-click reproduces identically outside a Playwright dblclick. QA reported it as always reproducible by hand; the modal overlay mounts on the first click at z-index 3000 (Modal.tsx:35), so the second click's exact hit path is the one thing this plan could not exercise without a browser.
